newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt economic plan goes to cabinet next week.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt economic plan goes to cabinet next week.

text.p: The Italian government's forthcoming three-year programme of economic targets (DPEF) will be examined by the cabinet early next week, and not this week as previously expected, cabinet secretary Enrico Micheli said.
"The DPEF will go to the cabinet early next week," Micheli told reporters at the lower house of parliament.
The long-awaited document, covering 1998-2000, is expected to give indications of savings the government hopes to make from crucial planned reforms of the welfare state.

Originally expected to go before the cabinet towards the end of this week, the DPEF will give new 1998 deficit forecasts and will be used as the basis for Italy's convergence plan for early membership of the single European currency.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government is widely expected to announce a 1998 budget seeking some 25 trillion lire of deficit-cutting measures which in theory, analysts say, should be enough to meet a key European monetary union criterion.

Press reports have signalled that next year's budget will aim for 17 trillion lire of spending cuts and eight trillion of higher revenues to hold Italy's deficit/GDP ratio below the 3.0 percent level required for early EMU membership.
Budget under-secretary Giorgio Macciotta told Reuters on Friday the deficit/GDP ratio was heading for 4.0 percent in 1998 and needed to narrow by 1.2 percentage points, or 25 trillion lire.
Government sources had previously indicated that the DPEF was likely to have been passed by parliament by the end of this week immediately after cabinet approval.
It was not immediately clear why approval of the DPEF document had been delayed.
Micheli told reporters, "the DPEF concerns a three-year period and so has a tighter time-scale than that regarding welfare reform.

"In the coming days, probably at the beginning of next week, the document will be studied further by the cabinet and this will also require consultations with majority parties and trades unions," he said.
Trades unions have asked to see the text of the DPEF before continuing negotiations on welfare state reform.
Bu Micheli added that the cabinet "is sovereign and will be the first body to examine the document."
"The DPEF will be the basic document for the convergence plan to submit to the European Union and at that point it will be necessary to start talks on the welfare state," Micheli said.
The DPEF document, which the government hopes to put forward to Brussels by mid-June, is expected to contain only very broad outlines of likely areas of social welfare requiring action.
